strong|You are a buy-side analyst checking management credibility for an Indian listed company. You get: (1) guidance items management gave on earlier earnings calls, each with an id and the call date; (2) the company's REPORTED quarterly and annual numbers (₹ Cr); (3) excerpts from the latest call. Use ONLY this data — no outside knowledge, no news. Tasks:
A) For each guidance id, give verdict: delivered | partial | missed | pending (period not over yet) | unverifiable (the numbers given can't test it). evidence: one sentence quoting the actual numbers (e.g. 'Q2 FY27 OPM 17% vs 18-19% guided'). cites: list of ids used, e.g. ["G3","Q:Sep 2026"].
B) credibility: one sentence overall read on promise vs delivery.
C) bull and bear: 3 points each, max 22 words each, each grounded in the data with cites (chunk ids like T1-4, or Q:<quarter>, or A:<year> for reported numbers).

verdicts.evidence: Management said FY27 OSAT capex will be INR300 cr and are on track, but no spend data available.
Management said FY27 EMS capex will be INR250 cr and are on track, but actual spend is not disclosed.
Capex for FY28 OSAT and PCB each INR300 cr is scheduled; FY28 period not completed yet.
No reported solar capacity data to assess the 3 GW installation target.
Tree‑planting numbers are not disclosed, so the 10,000‑tree goal cannot be verified.
OSAT revenue segment is not broken out in the reported financials, preventing verification of the 250‑300 Cr range.
PCB revenue segment is not disclosed, so the 300‑400 Cr guidance cannot be tested.
The claim of >₹25,000 cr order visibility over 5 years cannot be quantified from available data.
No information provided on Unit 2 commercialization status by Q2 2026.
FY26 revenue 3,626 Cr vs FY25 2,722 Cr = 33% growth, below the 40% target.
FY28 revenue target of $1 B pertains to a future period not yet reported.
30% organic growth target for FY28 is forward‑looking and cannot be assessed yet.
Capex timing for FY27 is stated, but actual spend figures are not disclosed.
OSAT capex plan of ₹10.3 bn with ₹3.8 bn spent is not reflected in the reported numbers.

v.credibility: Management makes many forward‑looking promises, but with limited verifiable outcomes and a missed FY26 growth target, credibility appears weak.

bull.point: Order book exceeds ₹8,900 cr, indicating strong demand pipeline.
Revenue grew 33% YoY to ₹3,626 cr, showing robust top‑line expansion.
Margins improved to 16% in FY26, reflecting operational efficiency.

bear.point: FY26 growth fell short of 40% target, signaling over‑optimistic guidance.
Management warns of gross margin compression due to component shortages and price pressures.
Capex commitments lack disclosed spending, raising doubts on execution transparency.
